articles.title: ‘Borges and Me’ Review: Gentle, Nostalgic Literary Road Movie Is More Perky Than Poetic
articles.summary: American author Jay Parini’s 2020 memoir “Borges and Me: An Encounter” read as a charming extension of an anecdote any writer would dine out on for the rest of their life: the tale of how Parini, as a college student in the 1970s, was somehow partnered on a winding road trip through the Scottish…
body: Revered Argentine writer Jose Luis Borges is rendered a colorful, quirky agent to a young writer's creative and romantic awakening in Marc Turteltaub's amiable, loosely biographical film.

Audiences might relate to some extent. In a sprightly performance rife with oddball mannerisms, Gnecco gives Borges equal parts impish wisdom, earthy vulgarity and childlike wonder, rarely letting a moment’s silence go unfilled with eager chatter. When the virginal Parini — who thus far has read romantic poetry without truly feeling it — hits it off with smart, kindly pub worker Ailith (a wonderful Freya Mavor) and they steal away for a time, the film positively breathes in the old man’s absence.

articles.title: Venice Film Festival Jury Press Conference ‘Probably Not’ Happening Due to Scheduling, Will Replace Event With Welcome Cocktails for Journalists
articles.summary: The Venice Film Festival is weighing scrapping its traditional opening jury press conference on the Lido. The festival, which kicks off Sept. 2 with the world premiere of Danny Boyle’s “Ink,” told Variety that the presser will “probably not” take place, citing a scheduling conflict, and said a…
body: The news comes just days after Nobel Prize-winning author Annie Ernaux, Pink Floyd co-founder Roger Waters and filmmakers including Matteo Garrone and Isabel Coixet signed an open letter urging the Venice Biennale and film festival to take “concrete action in support of Palestine.” The letter was organized by the Venice4Palestine collective, which similarly targeted the festival last year and had urged the event’s organizers to withdraw invitations to Gerard Butler and Gal Gadot over their previous support for Israel.

Venice artistic director Alberto Barbera has described this year’s lineup as Venice’s “most political” in recent years, with films tackling war, Palestine, immigration, climate change and shrinking political freedoms. Earlier this week, the fest added “NAZA,” a new hot-button documentary from “No Other Land” directors Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor, to the Venice competition lineup.

articles.title: Heidi Montag Recalls Dolly Parton Defending Her Amid Plastic Surgery Criticism
articles.summary: "When I was at one of the hardest and most criticized moment of my life after my plastic surgery, Dolly was one of the only people in the industry who didn't take the opportunity to drag me down," 'The Hills' shared on X.
body: Heidi Montag is remembering the kindness the late Dolly Parton showed her during one of the most heavily criticized periods of her life.
Following news of Parton’s death earlier this week, Montag took to X on Friday night to pay tribute to the country music legend, recalling how Parton defended her after she underwent plastic surgery.
According to Montag, she recalled that Parton said at the time, “I had probably done the same thing if I was her age and could afford it, if I thought I needed it.”

In 2009, Montag famously underwent 10 plastic surgery procedures in one day, including breast augmentation, a nose job revision and chin reduction. She faced intense scrutiny over the procedures, with the aftermath documented on The Hills, including a heartbreaking scene in which she revealed her new appearance to her mother.
points: Heidi Montag is remembering the kindness the late Dolly Parton showed her during one of the most heavily criticized periods of her life.

articles.title: Shailene Woodley Recalls Her “Dream” Role as Mary Jane Being Cut From ‘The Amazing Spider-Man 2’
articles.summary: "Spider-Man's my favorite superhero; Mary Jane was my favorite character growing up. So, when I got it, I was like, 'This is so exciting!'" the actress said before adding that she and Andrew Garfield filmed three scenes together that didn't make it into the 2014 movie.
body: Shailene Woodley is reflecting on the time her “dream” role as Mary Jane Watson was cut from The Amazing Spider-Man 2.

Speaking with the SAG-AFTRA Foundation’s Conversations recently, Woodley shared her reaction to learning that her scenes with Andrew Garfield, who starred as Peter Parker/Spider-Man, had been cut from the final film. The actress said she didn’t find out until about a year after she had finished filming the scenes for the Sony Pictures movie, which was released in theaters in May 2014.
Woodley said she was told the filmmakers planned to introduce Mary Jane after Peter’s relationship with Gwen Stacy, played by Stone, came to an end.

The Hollywood Reporter reported in 2013 that Woodley’s scenes had been cut from the film. At the time, director Marc Webb said the decision was made to streamline the story and focus on Peter and Gwen’s relationship.

articles.title: Before Project Hail Mary, Sandra Huller Appeared In A Deeply Underrated Sci-Fi Movie On Netflix
articles.summary: Before Sandra Hüller nabbed an Oscar nomination, she starred in this fantastic science-fiction movie with Dan Stevens that you can stream on Netflix.
body: "I'm Your Man" begins with the film's protagonist, Alma (Maren Eggert), having a conversation with a devastatingly handsome man named Tom (Dan Stevens) at a dance club. Alma asks Tom about math and poetry, odd topics to cover while at the club. When Tom asks her to dance, he begins repeating the same phrases over and over. It turns out that Tom is a high-tech android, and Alma was giving him a Turing test.

Alma, you see, has been asked to test the humanity of a new line of ultra-human robots being built to serve as ersatz romantic partners. After Tom's glitches are fixed, he is sent home with Alma, where he attempts to charm her 24 hours a day. He is her man. Sandra Hüller plays the unnamed employee of the android company that has issued Tom for testing. It's a pretty damn great movie that's currently playing on Netflix.
points: Before Sandra Hüller nabbed an Oscar nomination, she starred in this fantastic science-fiction movie with Dan Stevens that you can stream on Netflix.

articles.title: Not Interstellar, Not The Martian: This Space Movie Is A Must-Watch For Sci-Fi Fans
articles.summary: This underrated science-fiction film is a must-watch, and it's a shame it didn't get the attention it deserved upon release.
body: Science Fiction movies aren't relegated to the realm of space, but some of the very best that the genre has to offer make use of life beyond our little blue planet. "Interstellar" has been hailed as Christopher Nolan's emotional masterpiece in a filmography full of great movies, particularly in the realm of sci-fi. "The Martian" is one of the best works in director Ridley Scott's impressive career, particularly in his later years. But we're here to talk about another must-watch within the genre.

And we're not going to recommend a "Star Wars" or "Star Trek" movie. We're not going to talk about something glaringly obvious, particularly for fans of movies like "Interstellar" or "The Martian," which are very optimistic works of sci-fi. For that reason, we're not going to prop up "Project Hail Mary," which features an outstanding Ryan Gosling in one of the best sci-fi movies in recent memory, if not ever. No, we're going to talk about a much darker, far more overlooked gem from the 2000s. Specifically, Danny Boyle's "Sunshine."
points: This underrated science-fiction film is a must-watch, and it's a shame it didn't get the attention it deserved upon release.

articles.title: Chris Pratt’s $200M Sci-Fi Action Epic Is Officially Invading Prime Video
articles.summary: Chris Pratt is a man who's well versed in both the concept of saving the world and dealing with some mad sci-fi business. After all, this is a man who attempted to save humanity as Star Lord and who also tried to, you know, stop dinosaurs from eating us all.
body: Take the military carnage of Starship Troopers, throw in the time-bending premise of Edge of Tomorrow, and you’ve got The Tomorrow War. The movie begins when a group of time travelers arrives from the year 2051 with some fairly catastrophic news: Humanity is losing a global war against a deadly alien species known as the White Spikes. Humanity’s only hope is to transport soldiers and civilians from the present into the future to join the fight. Among those drafted is former Green Beret and science teacher Dan Forester (Pratt), whose mission becomes deeply personal when he discovers what has happened to his family in the decades ahead.

Alongside Pratt, The Tomorrow War stars Yvonne Strahovski ( The Handmaid’s Tale ) as Muri Forester, J.K. Simmons ( Whiplash ) as James Forester, Betty Gilpin ( GLOW ) as Emmy Forester, Sam Richardson (Veep ) as Charlie, Edwin Hodge ( The Purge ) as Dorian, Jasmine Mathews ( The Man From Toronto ) as Lieutenant Hart and Ryan Kiera Armstrong ( Firestarter ) as young Muri.
Your answers point to the world your instincts were built for. This is the universe your temperament, your survival instincts, and your particular brand of stubbornness were made for.

articles.title: Every 2026 Universal Studios Halloween Horror Nights Maze Ranked
articles.summary: From deadly demogorgons to the immortal Ozzy Osbourne, here's every maze at the 2026 Universal Studios Halloween Horror Nights, ranked.
body: Halloween Horror Nights at the Universal Orlando Resort is considered by many genre movie fans and haunt aficionados to be the preeminent haunted house event in the nation. This year's event, Halloween Horror Nights 35, lives up to that storied reputation. Once the sun sets, the park becomes overrun with scare actors and 10 unique haunted houses open their doors to terrified guests. The production values are always sky-high, the commitment to the bit from the actors always admirable, and the overall breadth of the experience generally overwhelming. In a good way, of course.

I was invited by Universal to check out Halloween Horror Nights 35, and because this is an article on the internet, you surely know what that means: I took it upon myself to rank all 10 of the new houses, which consist of five original houses and five houses based on existing movies, TV shows, and concepts. This ranking does not include the various scare zones that populate the streets around the park, but here's an honorable mention for "Downtown Clown Town," which is exactly what it sounds like and delighted me so much that I bought a souvenir t-shirt bearing its name.

articles.title: Coyote Vs Acme Proves One Thing About Modern Looney Tunes Movies
articles.summary: Coyote Vs Acme, like The Day the Earth Blew Up before it, proves that you can make a successful Looney Tunes movie without focusing on Bugs Bunny.
body: It's finally here, the motion picture event of 2026. After what felt like a personal crusade from Warner Bros. Discovery and David Zaslav to deprive children around the world from having any fun whatsoever, not only canning the fully-finished "Coyote vs Acme" but also deciding that no other studio would be able to pay money to release the film, unlikely saviors Ketchup Entertainment are finally unleashing the live-action/animation hybrid to the masses.

The movie is a triumph and the perfect film for 2026, a staunchly anti-corporation and anti-monopoly movie that's essentially "Who Framed Roger Rabbit" meets "Erin Brockovich." Though the animation could be a bit sharper, this is by no means a "Space Jam" scenario (sorry, fellow millennials), because the writing is on point. These are the Looney Tunes you know and love, with Samy Burch's screenplay (based on a story by Burch, James Gunn and Jeremy Slater) capturing the looniness, the over-the-top personalities, and the heart of the classic cartoon characters. Meanwhile, Eric Bauza continues to show he is the heir apparent to Mel Blanc, voicing virtually all the male Looney Tunes seamlessly.
points: Coyote Vs Acme, like The Day the Earth Blew Up before it, proves that you can make a successful Looney Tunes movie without focusing on Bugs Bunny.
